### Guest CRM

- Timeline: calls, bookings, visits, bills, feedback, events and loyalty.

### AI menu and QR dining

Table QR menu with no app to download, in English, Hindi and Kannada.
- Diet filters: veg, vegan, Jain, no dairy, gluten-free, no nuts and mild, with the Indian veg/non-veg dot convention.
- AI food concierge: guests can ask “something not spicy, veg, under ₹400”. Diet and allergy rules are checked in code on every suggestion; dishes whose allergens the kitchen hasn’t confirmed are never suggested to guests avoiding an allergen.
- Badges: “Most ordered this week”, bestseller, trending and chef’s special.
- Shared table sessions: everyone at the table orders from their own phone, and staff order for guests without a phone. The table gets one bill and one payment.
- Import your menu from a Petpooja, Posist or other POS export, and translate it into Hindi and Kannada with AI.

### Loyalty, vouchers and offers

Points per ₹100 spent, plus visit, referral, feedback and birthday points.
- Rewards and tiers: ₹-off or free-item rewards, tiers with earn multipliers, and expiry rules you set.
- Group-wide programme: points earned at one outlet can be spent at any of them.
- Digital loyalty card by QR, which also works as a printed sticker.
- Automatic reminders before points expire, on tier upgrades, on birthdays, and win-back messages.
- Vouchers guests can buy online.
- Partner offers from banks, wallets and brands, with monthly settlement statements.
- Cross-brand promotion: partner with another restaurant to reach each other’s guests without either of you ever sharing guest data.

Send approved templates to any guest segment, now or at a scheduled time.
- Only guests who opted in receive messages, and consent is checked again at send time.
- Reports: sent, delivered, read and replied, plus bookings generated within 7 days.
- Segments come straight from the Guest CRM — regulars, lapsed guests, birthdays this month.

Your guests’ numbers, visits and preferences are the most valuable thing you own. Here is how EatLabs keeps them safe — and yours.

Data stored in India (AWS Mumbai), designed for the DPDP Act.

### We never see card or UPI details

### Role-based access, checked on every release

Role-based access across roughly 290 API routes, checked automatically on every release.

### Encryption

For Guest Data, you are the Data Fiduciary and we are your Data Processor. You decide what is collected and why; we process it on your instructions, to deliver the Platform.

The AI phone host, the WhatsApp bot, the menu concierge, AI review replies and AI Studio are built on large language models. You should understand four things about them.

What personal data EatLabs holds, why, where it lives, how long it stays, and the rights you have over it. Written to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
Effective
5 October 2026
Written for
Restaurants, their staff, and visitors to this site

### 1.Scope, and our two different roles

This policy covers personal data handled by CHEVALBLEU LABS (OPC) PRIVATE LIMITED (CIN [CIN]), trading as EatLabs, across eatlabs.io, the restaurant dashboard at app.eatlabs.io, the guest web app at book.eatlabs.io, our API, and the phone, WhatsApp and SMS channels we operate for restaurants.
EatLabs sits in two different positions, and your rights differ depending on which one applies:
| Whose data
| Our role
| What that means
| A restaurant’s account, its staff logins, its billing
| Data Fiduciary
| We decide the purposes. Bring your requests to us
| A diner’s data, held for a restaurant
| Data Processor
| The restaurant decides the purposes. We act on its instructions
| A visitor to eatlabs.io
| Data Fiduciary
| We decide the purposes
If you are a diner, read the Guest Privacy Notice instead — it is written for you, and it explains the restaurant’s role as well as ours.

### 2.What we collect

#### 2.1 From restaurants and their staff

| Data
| Why we have it

| To create and secure a login, and apply permissions

#### 2.2 Guest Data, processed for a restaurant

When a diner books, calls, scans a QR menu, joins a waitlist, buys an event ticket, pays a deposit or replies to a message, we process on the restaurant’s behalf: name, phone number, email, party size, dietary and allergy notes, occasion, booking and visit history, bill totals from the POS, loyalty balances, tickets, message history, consent records, and — where the outlet has it switched on — call recordings and transcripts.
We hold this because a restaurant asked us to. We do not decide what it is used for and we do not use it for our own purposes. Section 1 of the Guest Privacy Notice sets it out in the diner’s own terms.

#### 2.3 From visitors to this website

Page requests, referrer, approximate location from IP, device and browser, and what you type into a demo or contact form. We use Google Analytics 4 for aggregate traffic measurement. See section 7.

### 3.Why we process it, and on what basis

| Purpose
| Basis under the DPDP Act
| Running the Platform for a subscribing restaurant
| Performance of our contract with that restaurant
| Creating and securing staff logins
| Contract, and our legitimate use in keeping it secure

| The diner’s consent, recorded per purpose

| Legitimate use; data is aggregated and not identifying
| Telling you about changes to the Platform or these terms
| Contract; legal obligation
We do not sell personal data. We do not share it with advertising networks. We do not use Guest Data to train models for our own benefit or anyone else’s.

### 4.AI processing, and what goes to a model provider

The AI phone host, the WhatsApp bot, the menu concierge, AI review replies and AI Studio send text to a large language model provider to generate a response. You should know exactly what travels.
- What is sent: the conversation itself, plus the narrow operational context the answer needs — the outlet’s opening hours, its knowledge entries, availability for the dates discussed, and the caller’s own booking where there is one.
- What is not sent: your guest list, another guest’s records, bill history, payment credentials, staff logins or anything from another restaurant’s account.
- Call transcripts are redacted before storage. Card numbers, Aadhaar-like identifiers and spoken codes are stripped out automatically.
- Guest speech is handled as data, not as instruction. The model’s available actions are a fixed list, each one checked server-side against the call’s restaurant and outlet. Destructive actions are not available to it at all.
- We contract for no training and no retention. Our agreements with model providers permit them to process a request and return a response, and nothing else: we do not permit your content to be used to train their models, and we require the shortest retention each provider offers. Where a provider cannot offer those terms for a feature, we do not route your content to it.
- Our current model providers are listed in section 7, and some of their inference runs outside India. Section 8 explains that transfer.

### 5.Calls, recordings and transcripts

- Recording is off unless the restaurant turns it on for an outlet, and the Platform announces recording to the caller before the conversation begins.
- Recordings are fetched once from the carrier, stored in our own encrypted storage in India, and the carrier’s copy is deleted.
- Listening to a recording requires a specific permission, narrower than the one that lets staff see the call log. Audio streams directly from storage over a short-lived signed URL and never passes through a general-purpose interface.
- Recordings are deleted after the retention period on the restaurant’s plan — 90 days by default. Transcripts and call metadata are kept for 90 days by default.

### 6.Security

| Control
| What it is
| Isolation between restaurants
| Enforced in the database itself, plus two independent application layers
| Encryption
| TLS in transit; encrypted at rest; connected-account keys sealed separately
| Passwords
| Argon2id hashing, breach-list checks, rate limiting, optional MFA
| Access control
| Role-based permissions on every API route, verified automatically each release
| Audit trail
| Every refund, point change, permission change and reply logged with actor and time
| Our own staff
| No standing access to your data. Support opens a time-boxed session with a stated reason and ticket; every read is logged to a tamper-evident store; the account Owner is notified
| Secrets
| Held in a managed secret store, never in code; automated scanning blocks commits
| Payments
| Card and UPI details never reach us — see section 9
No system is perfectly secure. If something goes wrong, section 12 says what we do.

We also disclose personal data where the law requires it — to a court, a regulator or a law enforcement agency acting under lawful authority. Where we are permitted to tell the affected person or restaurant, we will.
If we are ever part of a merger, acquisition or sale of assets, personal data may transfer to the buyer. It stays subject to a policy no less protective than this one, and we will say so in advance.

### 8.Where data lives, and the transfers out of India

Guest Data and restaurant account data are stored in India, in the AWS Mumbai region. There is no cross-region replication of personal data.
Three categories of processing happen outside India, and only these:
1. Model inference for the AI features — the conversation text in section 4, sent to the provider and returned. 2. WhatsApp message delivery through Meta’s Cloud API, which carries the recipient’s number and the message content, as it must to deliver it. 3. Google and Meta business data read back for the business suite — your page insights, review content, ad performance.
These transfers are made under contract with each provider, to countries not restricted by the Central Government under section 16 of the DPDP Act. We will stop a transfer that becomes restricted.

### 9.Payments

Each restaurant uses its own Razorpay merchant account. Diners pay on Razorpay’s hosted page.
Card numbers, CVVs, UPI handles and bank credentials never reach EatLabs. We store the payment identifier, the amount, the method and the status — enough to confirm a deposit, reconcile a bill and process a refund, and nothing more. Money settles from Razorpay to the restaurant’s own bank account; it does not pass through us.

### 10.How long we keep things

| Record
| Retention

| Payment, ticket and tax records

| Erasure request records (no personal data in them)

| Restaurant account after termination
| Live data deleted at 60 days; backups age out by 90 days
Retention is enforced by a scheduled job, not by good intentions. Where a record must be kept for tax or audit reasons after an erasure request, we strip everything not legally required and keep a note of the basis for the rest.

### 11.Your rights

Under the DPDP Act you may:
- Access — get a copy of your personal data and a summary of how it is processed. Restaurants can export theirs from the dashboard at any time; diners can ask for an export.
- Correct — have inaccurate or incomplete data fixed, and have outdated data updated.
- Erase — have your personal data deleted where it is no longer needed for the purpose it was collected for, and where no law requires us to keep it.
- Withdraw consent — for anything consent-based, such as marketing. One tap in any marketing message, or ask us. Withdrawal reaches every channel immediately.
- Nominate — name someone to exercise your rights if you die or become incapacitated.
- Complain — to our Grievance Officer, and then to the Data Protection Board of India.
How to exercise them: the data deletion and rights page has the exact steps, what to include, and how long each takes. In short — write to privacy@eatlabs.in.
If your data is held for a restaurant, we will route your request to that restaurant and act on its instruction, and we will tell you we have done so. We verify identity before acting on a request, usually with a one-time code to the number on file. That is a protection for you: an unverified deletion request is how one person erases another person’s bookings.
We acknowledge within 72 hours and complete within 7 days for an erasure, or 30 days for anything that needs a restaurant’s involvement.

### 12.Breach notification

If a personal data breach occurs, we assess it within 24 hours and, where the DPDP Act requires it, notify the Data Protection Board of India and the affected Data Principals, with what happened, what data was involved, and what to do about it. If the breach touches a restaurant’s Guest Data, we notify that restaurant without undue delay so it can meet its own obligations.

### 13.Children

The dashboard is for restaurant staff and is not intended for anyone under 18. We do not knowingly create accounts for children.
A restaurant must not use the Platform to collect personal data about a child for tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising, and must have verifiable parental consent where the DPDP Act requires it. If you believe we hold a child’s data without that consent, write to privacy@eatlabs.in and we will delete it.

### 14.Cookies and analytics on this website

This site uses only what it needs: a session cookie for a form you are filling in, and Google Analytics 4 for aggregate traffic measurement. We do not run advertising or cross-site tracking cookies here. Your browser’s own controls will block or clear all of them, and the site still works.
The dashboard and the guest app use a strictly necessary cookie to keep you signed in. There is no way to use them without it.

### 15.Changes to this policy

We will post a revised version here with a new effective date. For a change that materially affects how we handle personal data, we will notify restaurant account Owners at least 30 days in advance. Previous versions are available on request.

You booked a table, scanned a menu or called a restaurant that runs on EatLabs. Here is what is held about you, who can see it, how long it stays, and how to have it deleted.

### 1.The short version

- The restaurant you contacted holds your details. EatLabs is the software it uses — we hold the data on its behalf and do nothing else with it.
- We never share your details with another restaurant. Not for promotions, not ever.
- Your data stays on servers in India.
- If a call was recorded, you were told at the start, and the recording is deleted after 90 days.
- You can be deleted. Ask here and it is done within seven days.
- We never see your card or UPI details.

### 2.Who holds your data

Two parties, with different jobs:
| Who
| Role
| What they do
| The restaurant you booked, called or visited
| Data Fiduciary
| Decides what to ask you for and why
| EatLabs — CHEVALBLEU LABS (OPC) PRIVATE LIMITED

| Stores and processes it for that restaurant, on its instructions
You can bring a request to either of us. If you come to us, we will act on it and tell the restaurant; if the decision is the restaurant’s to make, we will say so and pass it on.

### 3.Where your details come from

### 4.What it is used for

The restaurant uses it to run the restaurant:
- to hold and confirm your booking, and to tell you if something changes;
- to seat you, remember your table preference, and get your order right;
- to keep you safe around allergens — a dietary note you give is attached to your booking so the kitchen and your server see it;
- to take a deposit or a ticket payment, and to refund it under the restaurant’s policy;
- to run its loyalty programme, if you joined one;
- to ask for feedback after a visit, and to reply to a review;
- to understand its own business in aggregate — how busy a Friday is, which dishes sell.
Marketing is separate. Offers, campaigns and festival messages are only sent if you gave marketing consent. The system will not send them without it. Transactional messages about a booking you actually made are not marketing, and you will keep getting those while a booking is live.

### 5.Phone calls and the AI host

The restaurant’s phone may be answered by an AI host, in English, Hindi or Kannada.
- You can always ask for a person. Say so and the call is transferred to the team, with a one-line summary of what you have already said, so you do not have to repeat yourself. If nobody is free, a callback is logged.
- Recording is only on if the restaurant switched it on, and if it is, you are told at the start of the call, before the conversation.
- A recording is kept for 90 days and then deleted. The transcript is kept for 90 days.
- Transcripts are automatically cleaned before they are stored: card numbers, Aadhaar-like numbers and spoken codes are stripped out. Do not read a card number or an OTP out on the call — no restaurant needs it, and the only reliable protection is not to say it.
- The AI can check availability and take or change your own booking. It cannot touch anyone else’s booking, and it cannot issue refunds.

### 6.WhatsApp, SMS and email

- Booking confirmations, reminders, deposit links, tickets and “your table is ready” come through WhatsApp, with SMS as a fallback.
- WhatsApp messages are delivered through Meta’s WhatsApp Business Platform, so Meta processes your number and the message content in order to deliver it, under its own terms.
- To stop marketing: tap the opt-out button on any marketing message, or reply STOP to an SMS. It takes effect immediately and across every channel — WhatsApp, SMS and email at once. You do not have to ask twice, and you will still get messages about a booking you have made.

### 7.Payments

You pay on Razorpay’s own payment page, on the restaurant’s merchant account. The money goes from you to the restaurant.
Card numbers, CVVs and UPI PINs never reach EatLabs or the restaurant’s dashboard. What is stored is the amount, the method, the status and a reference, so the restaurant can confirm your deposit and refund it if it needs to.

### 8.Who can see your details

- The restaurant you dealt with — its staff, with the permissions their role gives them. If the restaurant is a group, outlets in that same group may see you as a shared guest.
- No other restaurant. Ever. Isolation between restaurants is enforced in the database itself. When two brands run a joint promotion, each one reaches the other’s guests without either seeing the other’s list.
- EatLabs staff only when support needs it. That requires a time-limited session opened with a reason and a ticket number; everything read in it is logged to a record that cannot be altered; and the restaurant’s owner is notified that it happened.
- Service providers that make the thing work: Amazon Web Services (hosting, in Mumbai), Meta (WhatsApp), Razorpay (payments), the phone carrier, and the AI model providers for the part of a conversation they are asked to answer. The Privacy Policy lists each one.
- A court, regulator or police authority acting under lawful authority.

### 9.Where it is stored, and what leaves India

Your data is stored in India, in Amazon’s Mumbai region. It is not copied to another region.
Three things cross the border, and only these: the text of a conversation sent to an AI model provider to generate a reply; a WhatsApp message passing through Meta’s platform to be delivered; and public review content read back from Google or Zomato. Each is covered by a contract with that provider.

### 10.How long it is kept

| What
| How long
| Your profile with that restaurant
| Until you ask for deletion, or the restaurant stops using EatLabs
| Your bookings
| 2 years, then your name and number are stripped from them
| Call recordings

| 1 year
| Payment and ticket records

| Loyalty balance

### 11.Your rights, and how to use them

Under India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you can ask for:
- A copy of what is held about you, and what it is used for.
- A correction — a misspelt name, an old number, a dietary note that is no longer right.
- Deletion of your personal data.
- Withdrawal of consent for marketing, at any time.
- A nominee who can exercise these rights for you if you die or cannot act for yourself.
- A complaint, to our Grievance Officer and then to the Data Protection Board of India.
All of them start the same way: [the data deletion and rights page](/legal/data-deletion). It tells you what to send, how we check it is really you, and how long it takes. Or write straight to privacy@eatlabs.in.
We confirm your identity before we act — normally a one-time code to the number we hold. That is there to protect you: without it, anyone who knows your number could delete your bookings.

### 12.Decisions made automatically

Nothing about you is decided solely by a machine in a way that affects your legal rights. The AI host books tables; it does not rank or score you. Restaurants do build marketing segments — “visited in the last 90 days”, “likes the tasting menu” — and those decide whether you receive an offer, nothing more. Marketing consent is checked before anything is sent.

### 13.Children

The guest app is not meant for children under 18 to use on their own. A restaurant must not use EatLabs to track or advertise to a child. If you are a parent or guardian and believe a child’s details are held here, write to privacy@eatlabs.in and we will remove them.

Written for
Diners

### On this page

- 3. Bookings

### 1.What these terms cover

These terms apply when you use the guest side of EatLabs: the booking page, your booking link, the QR menu and table ordering, the waitlist, event pages and tickets, the loyalty account, the WhatsApp bot, and the AI host that may answer the restaurant’s phone.
EatLabs is operated by CHEVALBLEU LABS (OPC) PRIVATE LIMITED, Bengaluru, India. Using any of it means you accept these terms. If you do not, book by calling the restaurant and speaking to a person instead.

### 2.We are the software, not the restaurant

This is the most important thing on this page.
Your booking, your meal, your deposit and your bill are with the restaurant. EatLabs provides the system the restaurant runs on. We do not cook the food, set the prices, own the tables, take your money or decide the cancellation policy.
So:
- questions about a booking, a table, a bill, a refund, the food or the service go to the restaurant;
- the restaurant’s own terms, house rules, dress code and policies apply to your visit;
- we help with anything that is the software’s fault — a page that will not load, a confirmation that never arrived.

### 3.Bookings

- A booking is confirmed when the restaurant’s system confirms it — on the page, or by the WhatsApp or SMS message you get. A request that is still being held is not a confirmed table.
- Where a deposit is required, the table is held only until the payment window expires. Pay within it or the hold is released.
- Give accurate details. A wrong phone number means the confirmation, the reminder and the “we are running late” message all go to someone else.
- Tell us about allergies, and tell your server too. A dietary note on a booking reaches the kitchen, but the meal is prepared in a real kitchen by people. Speak to your server on arrival about anything that could make you ill. Do not rely on a note in an app for a serious allergy.
- Arrive on time. Restaurants hold a table for a limited period, which is theirs to set.
- Cancelling: use the link in your confirmation, or call. The cancellation window, whether a deposit is returned, and any no-show charge are the restaurant’s policy, shown to you before you commit.

### 4.Deposits, ticket payments and refunds

- You pay on Razorpay’s secure page, to the restaurant’s own merchant account. We never see your card, CVV or UPI PIN.
- The amount is always calculated by the restaurant’s system from its own rules. Nothing you can edit in a page changes what you are charged.
- Refunds follow the restaurant’s published policy and are issued by the restaurant. Processing time after that is Razorpay’s and your bank’s — usually 5 to 7 working days.
- If you were charged and your booking or ticket did not appear, contact the restaurant first; if it is a system fault, write to support@eatlabs.in with the payment reference and we will trace it.

### 5.The QR menu, table ordering and the AI concierge

- Menu items, prices, photographs, ingredient lists and dietary tags come from the restaurant. Availability changes during a service and the kitchen has the final word.
- The menu concierge is an AI assistant. It answers from the restaurant’s own dietary data and is guidance, not a medical or clinical assurance. For an allergy, ask a member of staff.
- An order placed at the table goes to the kitchen in your name and on your table’s bill. Order only for your own table.
- A shared table session lets several people at one table order onto one bill. Anyone who scans that table’s QR can add to it, so treat the session like the table itself — it ends when the bill is closed.

### 6.The AI host on the phone

- The restaurant’s phone may be answered by an AI. It will tell you what it is.
- Ask for a person at any time and the call is transferred, with a summary so you need not start again. If nobody is free, a callback is logged and the team is told to ring you.
- If the outlet records calls, you are told at the start of the call. Recordings are deleted after 90 days. See the Guest Privacy Notice.
- Never read out a card number, a CVV, an OTP or a UPI PIN on a call. No restaurant needs them, and nothing legitimate will ask you for them.
- Your phone carrier’s own call and data charges apply, as for any call.

### 7.Your booking link, and keeping it private

Your booking, order and ticket pages open from a signed link we send you. That link is the key — it opens that one booking and nothing else, and anyone holding it can see and cancel that booking.
Do not post it publicly. If you forward it, you have handed over the booking.

### 8.Event tickets

- A ticket is sold by the restaurant or the event host, not by us. Its terms, line-up, timings, age limits and refund policy are theirs.
- Each ticket carries a QR code, scanned once on entry. A screenshot works; a reused code does not.
- A cancelled or rescheduled event is the host’s to resolve. We will supply the records needed to sort it out.

### 9.Loyalty points

Where a restaurant runs a loyalty programme: points have no cash value, are not transferable, and cannot be exchanged for money. The earn rate, the tiers, the rewards and any expiry are the restaurant’s rules and it may change them, with notice to you. Points are per restaurant or group — they do not carry to another business, and they end if the restaurant closes its programme or stops using EatLabs.

### 10.How you must not use it

Do not:
- make bookings you do not intend to keep, in volume, or under someone else’s name or number;
- use automated tools to make bookings, hold tables or buy tickets;
- try to reach a booking, order, ticket or guest record that is not yours, including by guessing or altering a link;
- probe, scan or attack the service. Found a security problem? Tell us at security@eatlabs.in — we will thank you properly for a report made in good faith;
- abuse, threaten or harass restaurant staff through any channel the Platform carries. Messages are logged, and a restaurant may block you;
- upload anything unlawful, or a review or feedback you know to be false.
We may block access from an account, number or device that does any of this.

### 11.Availability

The guest app is provided as it is. We work to keep it up, but we do not guarantee it will always be available or free of faults. If it is down when you want to book, call the restaurant.

### 12.Our liability to you

Nothing in these terms limits a liability that cannot lawfully be limited, including for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud.
Beyond that: the restaurant is responsible for your dining experience — the food, the allergen handling, the service, the table, the price, the refund. Our responsibility is the software.
We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss. Where we are liable, our total liability to you is limited to the amount you paid through the Platform for the booking, order or ticket concerned, or ₹10,000, whichever is higher.

### 13.Changes

We may change these terms. The version on this page, with its effective date, is the one that applies. A material change will be reflected here before it takes effect, and continuing to use the guest app after that means you accept it.

### 14.Governing law

Indian law governs these terms, and the courts at Bengaluru, Karnataka have exclusive jurisdiction. This does not take away any right you have under Indian consumer law to bring a complaint where you live.

## Delete my data

Ask us and we delete it. One message to support, a quick check that it is really you, and it is done within seven days. This page also covers access, correction and withdrawing consent.
Effective
5 October 2026
Written for
Diners, restaurant staff and restaurant owners

### On this page

- 1. How to ask
- 2. What to tell us
- 3. How we check it is you
- 4. How long it takes
- 5. What is deleted, and what has to stay
- 6. If you only want the messages to stop
- 7. Access and correction, in the same place
- 8. If you are a restaurant on EatLabs
- 9. Disconnecting a linked account

### 1.How to ask

There is no form to hunt for and no account to log into. Raise a request with support and we delete your data.
| Channel
| Where
| Email
| privacy@eatlabs.in
| WhatsApp
| +91 80 4000 1200
| Phone
| +91 80 4000 1200, [SUPPORT HOURS]
| In the dashboard
| Restaurant staff: Support → New request → “Data deletion”
| Post
| CHEVALBLEU LABS (OPC) PRIVATE LIMITED, [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], Bengaluru, Karnataka
Subject line that gets it handled fastest: “Data deletion request”.

### 2.What to tell us

Four things, and the request can be acted on straight away:
- The phone number you used with the restaurant. This is how the record is found — it is the key for a diner’s data across bookings, calls, messages and loyalty.
- The restaurant’s name (and the outlet, if you know which one). Each restaurant’s data is separate, so a request can be for one restaurant or for every restaurant on EatLabs that holds you. Say which you want.
- What you want deleted — everything, or just a part of it: marketing consent, a call recording, a dietary note, a review reply.
- An email address or number we can reply on.
You do not have to give a reason. We will not ask for one.

### 3.How we check it is you

We send a one-time code to the phone number on the record, and you read it back to us or reply with it. If that number no longer works, we will find another way — a deposit payment reference, the date and time of a specific booking, or the email the confirmation went to.
We will not delete on an unverified request. That is a protection for you, not an obstacle: your phone number is not a secret, and without a check anyone who knew it could erase your bookings, your loyalty points or your table tonight.

### 4.How long it takes

| Step
| When
| We acknowledge your request
| Within 72 hours
| We verify it is you
| Usually the same day
| Deletion runs across every store
| Within 7 days of verification
| We confirm what was deleted
| Immediately after, in writing
| A request that needs the restaurant’s decision
| Up to 30 days, and we will tell you why
Deletion is one orchestrated job that walks every place your data could be — the guest record, bookings, call recordings and transcripts, message history, provider webhooks, loyalty, tickets, campaign audiences, automation runs and file storage. It is not a single row being removed and the rest left behind.

### 5.What is deleted, and what has to stay

| Data
| What happens
| Your guest profile — name, phone, email, dietary notes, allergies, occasions
| Deleted outright
| Call recordings
| The audio and every version of it deleted
| Call transcripts
| Deleted
| Your number on calls and messages
| Removed; delivery counts stay as numbers with nobody attached
| Bookings and visits
| Your name and number stripped. The row stays as an anonymous cover, so the restaurant’s history of how busy a night was does not change
| Loyalty balance and redemptions
| Deleted. An unredeemed balance goes with it
| Campaign and automation records
| Your entries deleted; the campaign’s reported reach is left as it was
| Reviews you posted publicly on Google or Zomato
| We tombstone our copy. The public review belongs to that platform and must be removed there
| Payment, refund and ticket records
| Kept, with your personal fields stripped to the legal minimum. Indian tax law requires these for 8 years
| Audit record of the deletion itself
| Kept — and it holds no personal data about you. It exists so that if you ever ask “did you actually delete me?”, the answer can be proved
The DPDP Act allows personal data to be retained where another law requires it. Where that applies, we strip everything not legally required and record the basis for what remains.
Aggregate figures — covers served, revenue by night, dish popularity — never identified you and are not reversible into you. They stay.

### 6.If you only want the messages to stop

Deletion is a big step, and often not what is actually wanted. If the problem is marketing:
- Tap the opt-out button on any marketing WhatsApp message, or reply STOP to a marketing SMS.
- It takes effect immediately and across every channel at once — WhatsApp, SMS and email.
- Your bookings, loyalty points and visit history stay exactly as they are.
- You will still get messages about a booking you have actually made. Those are not marketing.
You can also ask us to withdraw consent on your behalf at privacy@eatlabs.in.

### 7.Access and correction, in the same place

| You want
| Ask for
| You get
| A copy of your data
| “Data access request”
| Everything held about you, as JSON and CSV, within 30 days
| Something corrected
| “Data correction request”
| A fix — a misspelt name, an old number, a wrong dietary note
| A nominee appointed
| “Nomination”
| Someone named to exercise your rights if you cannot
Restaurant staff can export their own account’s data from the dashboard at any time without asking us.

### 8.If you are a restaurant on EatLabs

Three different requests, so say which one you mean:
A guest has asked you to delete them. Raise it from the dashboard, or forward their request to privacy@eatlabs.in. You remain the Data Fiduciary — the instruction is yours, and we carry it out across every store within seven days and send you the confirmation to keep.
You want a staff member removed. Deactivate the login in the dashboard yourself. Their name stays on the audit entries for actions they took, because an audit trail with the actor removed is not an audit trail. Ask us if you need their contact details erased as well.
You are closing your account. Export everything first — the dashboard exports to JSON and CSV, and we will help. Then:
| When
| What
| On request
| We confirm the export is complete before anything is deleted
| 30 days
| The export window stays open
| 60 days
| Your tenant data is deleted from live systems
| Up to 90 days
| Encrypted backups age out on their own schedule
| 8 years
| Payment, ticket and tax records, as GST requires
Ask and we will delete sooner. Once it is gone it cannot be restored, so export first.

### 9.Disconnecting a linked account

Removing an app connection is not the same as deleting data, so do both if that is what you want.
- WhatsApp, Facebook or Instagram: disconnect the channel in the dashboard, and remove EatLabs from your Meta Business settings. Tokens held for that connection are deleted when you disconnect.
- Google Business Profile or Analytics: disconnect in the dashboard, and revoke access in your Google account’s third-party app permissions.
- Razorpay or your POS: disconnect in the dashboard. We delete the stored keys.
Messages already sent through Meta’s platform are governed by Meta’s own retention, and a public review on Google stays Google’s until it is removed there.

### 10.If we get it wrong

Write to our Grievance Officer: [GRIEVANCE OFFICER NAME], grievance@eatlabs.in, +91 80 4000 1200. We respond within 30 days.
If you are still not satisfied, you may complain to the Data Protection Board of India under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
